title.en: Volume 353 Biographies 140: Da Chun | son: Sa Bin Tu, Tie Bao younger brother: Yu Bao, He Ying, Jue Luo Gui Fang
title.raw: 卷353 列傳一百四十 达椿|子：萨彬图 铁保弟：玉保 和瑛 觉罗桂芳

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十

translations.literal: Biographies 140
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 140

sentences.zh: 達椿子薩彬圖鐵保弟玉保和瑛覺羅桂芳

translations.literal: Da Chun; his son Sa Bintu; Tie Bao; Tie Bao's younger brother Yu Bao; He Ying; Jueluo Guifang
translations.idiomatic: Da Chun (and his son Sa Bintu), Tie Bao (and his younger brother Yu Bao), He Ying, and Jueluo Guifang

sentences.zh: 達椿，字香圃，烏蘇氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Da Chun, style name Xiangpu, of the Wusu clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Da Chun, courtesy name Xiangpu, of the Wusu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年進士，選庶吉士，散館授戶部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: In the 25th year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor, and upon leaving the Hanlin Academy was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, later promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Qianlong 25, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after leaving the Academy was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, then promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 歷翰林院侍講、侍讀、國子監祭酒、詹事府詹事、大理寺卿。

translations.literal: He successively served as Hanlin lecturer, Hanlin reader, chancellor of the Imperial Academy, grand tutor in the Household of the Heir Apparent, and president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Hanlin lecturer and reader, chancellor of the Imperial Academy, grand tutor in the Heir Apparent's household, and president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，入直上書房，充四庫全書總閱，累擢禮部侍郎，兼副都統。

translations.literal: In the 29th year he entered the Imperial Study, served as chief reviewer for the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, and was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of Rites, concurrently holding the post of vice commander of a banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 29 he joined the Imperial Study and served as chief reviewer for the Siku Quanshu, eventually rising to vice minister of Rites while also holding a vice commandership of a banner.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，坐會同四譯館屋壞，斃朝鮮使臣，革職留任。

translations.literal: In the 45th year, because the building of the Joint Four Translation Offices collapsed and killed a Korean envoy, he was stripped of office but retained on duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 45 a collapse at the Joint Four Translation Offices killed a Korean envoy; he was dismissed from his post but kept at his duties.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，左遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the 54th year he was demoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he was demoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 達椿直內廷，不附和珅，數媒孽其短，以曠直褫職，仍留上書房效力行走。

translations.literal: Da Chun served in the inner court and would not attach himself to Heshen; Heshen repeatedly slandered his faults; on grounds of absenteeism and bluntness his office was removed, yet he remained to serve in the Imperial Study.
translations.idiomatic: Da Chun served in the inner court and refused to align with Heshen, who repeatedly traduced him; he was stripped of rank for absenteeism and bluntness but was kept on in the Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 尋授翰林院侍講學士，复迭以大考降黜授檢討。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Hanlin associate lecturer, but again and again was demoted through the triennial examination to the post of reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hanlin associate lecturer, yet repeated poor showings in the triennial examination reduced him again and again to reviser.

sentences.zh: 仁宗知其屈抑，至嘉慶四年，詔：「達椿因曠班被譴，其過輕，當時劉墉亦緣此降官；

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong knew he had been wronged; by the 4th year of Jiaqing an edict stated: 'Da Chun was censured for absenteeism; the fault was slight. At that time Liu Yong was also demoted for the same reason;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor knew he had been unfairly held down; in Jiaqing 4 an edict declared: 'Da Chun was punished for absenteeism, a light offense; Liu Yong had been demoted for the same reason at the time;

sentences.zh: 今劉墉已為大學士，達椿尚未遷擢，加恩補授內閣學士兼副都統。

translations.literal: now Liu Yong is already a grand secretary, while Da Chun has still not been promoted; bestow favor and appoint him in addition as Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently vice commander of a banner.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong is now a grand secretary while Da Chun has still not been advanced; let favor be shown and let him be appointed Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently vice commander of a banner.'

sentences.zh: 」子薩彬圖，時亦同官，命達椿班次列薩彬圖之前。

translations.literal: ' His son Sa Bintu held the same rank at the time; Da Chun was ordered to take precedence over Sa Bintu in court order.
translations.idiomatic: ' His son Sa Bintu held the same post; the emperor ordered Da Chun to rank ahead of his son in court precedence.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部、吏部侍郎，兼翰林院掌院學士，擢左都御史兼都統，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice minister of Rites and Personnel, concurrently chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, was promoted to left censor-in-chief with concurrent command of a banner, and was transferred to minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of Rites and of Personnel, concurrently headed the Hanlin Academy, was promoted to left censor-in-chief with a banner command, and became minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the 6th year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 6 he presided over the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the 7th year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiaqing 7.

sentences.zh: 薩彬圖，乾隆四十五年進士，授戶部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Sa Bintu, jinshi in the 45th year of Qianlong, was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Sa Bintu, who took his jinshi in Qianlong 45, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 典貴州鄉試，改歷翰詹，累遷內閣學士兼副都統。

translations.literal: He presided over the Guizhou provincial examination, then transferred through Hanlin and Household posts, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently vice commander of a banner.
translations.idiomatic: After supervising the Guizhou provincial examination he moved through Hanlin and Household offices, eventually becoming Grand Secretariat academician with a concurrent banner vice commandership.

sentences.zh: 和珅既伏法，仁宗不欲株連興獄，而薩彬圖屢疏言和珅財產多寄頓隱匿，有嘗管金銀使女四名，請獨至慎刑司訊鞫。

translations.literal: After Heshen had been executed, Emperor Renzong did not wish to extend prosecutions, yet Sa Bintu repeatedly memorialized that much of Heshen's property had been deposited and concealed, and that there were four maidservants who had managed his gold and silver; he asked to interrogate them alone at the Imperial Prison.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heshen had been executed, the emperor wished to avoid widening the purge, but Sa Bintu repeatedly reported that much of Heshen's wealth had been hidden away and that four maidservants who had managed his bullion should be examined alone at the Imperial Prison.

sentences.zh: 詔嚴斥之，命從王大臣訊，不得實，議革職，予七品筆帖式，效力萬年吉地。

translations.literal: An edict sternly rebuked him and ordered him to follow the princely ministers in the inquiry; nothing was proved; it was proposed to dismiss him from office and grant him a seventh-rank clerkship, to serve at the Eternal Felicity mausoleum site.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked him and had him join the princely commissioners' inquiry; when nothing was substantiated, he was stripped of office and given a seventh-rank clerkship at the imperial mausoleum works.

sentences.zh: 尋以其父年老，召還京，授戶部主事，累擢倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon, because his father was old, he was recalled to the capital, appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and repeatedly promoted to vice minister in charge of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as his father was elderly, he was recalled to Beijing, reappointed a Revenue clerk, and rose to vice minister overseeing the capital granaries.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出為漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the 12th year he went out as director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 12 he was appointed director-general of the Grand Canal grain transport.

sentences.zh: 逾三歲，京倉虧缺事覺，降光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: After more than three years, shortages in the capital granaries came to light; he was demoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, shortfalls in the capital granaries were exposed and he was demoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遷盛京戶部侍郎，十六年，坐奉天災民流徙出邊，褫職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of Revenue at Mukden; in the 16th year, because famine in Fengtian drove people to flee beyond the border, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Mukden as vice minister of Revenue; in Jiaqing 16 he was dismissed after famine in Fengtian drove refugees across the border.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 鐵保，字冶亭，棟鄂氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Tie Bao, style name Yeting, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Bao, courtesy name Yeting, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 先世姓覺羅，稱為趙宋之裔，後改今氏。

translations.literal: His ancestors bore the surname Jueluo and were said to be descendants of the Zhao-Song; later they changed to the present clan name.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had borne the surname Jueluo and were claimed as descendants of the Song house of Zhao before adopting the present clan name.

sentences.zh: 父誠泰，泰宁鎮總兵，世為將家。

translations.literal: His father Cheng Tai was regional commander at Taipingzhen; for generations the family had been a military house.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng Tai was regional commander at Taipingzhen; the family had been soldiers for generations.

sentences.zh: 鐵保折節讀書，年二十一，成乾隆三十七年進士，授吏部主事，襲恩騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Tie Bao curbed himself to study; at age twenty-one he passed the jinshi examination in the 37th year of Qianlong, was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and inherited the hereditary rank of Enqiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Bao bent himself to scholarship; at twenty-one he took his jinshi in Qianlong 37, entered the Ministry of Personnel as a principal clerk, and inherited the hereditary Enqiwei rank.

sentences.zh: 於曹司中介然孤立，意有不可，爭辯勿撓。

translations.literal: Among the ministry offices he stood conspicuously alone; when he thought something wrong, he argued and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: In the ministries he stood apart; whenever he thought a matter wrong, he argued and would not back down.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿桂屢薦之，遷郎中，擢少詹事，因事罷。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Agui repeatedly recommended him; he was promoted to director, then to junior tutor in the Heir Apparent's household, and was dismissed over an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Agui repeatedly recommended him; he rose to director and then junior tutor in the Heir Apparent's household before being dismissed over a dispute.

sentences.zh: 尋補戶部員外郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was reappointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed a Revenue vice director and transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 擢翰林院侍講學士，仍兼吏部行走，歷侍讀學士、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin associate lecturer, still concurrently serving in the Ministry of Personnel, and passed through reader and Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin associate lecturer while still serving in Personnel, then reader and Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，遷禮部侍郎，兼副都統。

translations.literal: In the 54th year he was transferred to vice minister of Rites, concurrently vice commander of a banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he became vice minister of Rites with a concurrent banner vice commandership.

sentences.zh: 校射中的，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the archery review he hit the target and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He hit the mark in the archery review and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 調吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，奏劾司員，帝責其過當，左遷內閣學士，轉盛京兵部、刑部侍郎，兼奉天府尹。

translations.literal: In the 4th year of Jiaqing he memorialized impeaching a subordinate official; the emperor rebuked him for excess and demoted him to Grand Secretariat academician, then transferred him to vice minister of War and Punishments at Mukden, concurrently Fengtian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he impeached a subordinate; the emperor called his action excessive and demoted him to Grand Secretariat academician, then sent him to Mukden as vice minister of War and Punishments while also making him Fengtian prefect.

sentences.zh: 尋復召為吏部侍郎，出為漕運總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was again summoned as vice minister of Personnel and went out as director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice minister of Personnel and appointed director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 五年，值車駕將幸盛京，疏請御道因舊址，勿闢新道；

translations.literal: In the 5th year, as the imperial procession was about to visit Mukden, he memorialized asking that the imperial route follow the old line and not open a new road;
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5, as the court prepared to visit Mukden, he urged that the imperial route follow the old road rather than cut a new one;

sentences.zh: 裁革餽送扈從官員土儀；

translations.literal: to abolish local gifts presented to accompanying officials;
translations.idiomatic: to abolish local gifts to officials in the entourage;

sentences.zh: 禁從官妄拿車馬：上嘉納之。

translations.literal: and to forbid attendants from seizing carts and horses at will: the emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: and to forbid attendants from requisitioning carts and horses at will—the emperor approved these proposals warmly.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷廣東巡撫，調山東。

translations.literal: In the 7th year he was transferred to governor of Guangdong, then to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 7 he was made governor of Guangdong, then transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 河決衡家樓，詔預籌運道。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke at Hengjialou; an edict ordered advance planning for the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst at Hengjialou, he was ordered to plan alternate transport routes in advance.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，漕運迅速，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the 3rd month of the 9th year, because grain transport was swift, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jiaqing 9, swift grain transport earned him the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋以水淺船遲，革職留任。

translations.literal: Soon, because the water was shallow and boats were delayed, he was dismissed from office but retained on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon shallow water slowed the fleet; he was dismissed but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢兩江總督，命覆鞫安徽壽州武舉張大有妒姦毒斃族侄獄，蘇州知府週鍔受賄輕縱，及初彭齡為安徽巡撫，勘實置法。

translations.literal: In the 10th year he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Jiangs and ordered to re-examine the case in which Zhang Dayou, a military licentiate of Shouzhou in Anhui, had poisoned his clansman's son out of jealousy over an affair, and Zhou E, prefect of Suzhou, had taken bribes and treated the matter lightly; when Chu Pengling became governor of Anhui, the facts were verified and the law applied.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 he was made governor-general of the Two Jiangs and told to reopen the case of Zhang Dayou, a Shouzhou military licentiate who had poisoned a kinsman's son in a jealous affair, and of Suzhou prefect Zhou E, who had taken bribes and let the crime go lightly; once Chu Pengling became Anhui governor, the facts were proved and justice done.

sentences.zh: 鐵保坐失察，褫宮銜，降二品頂戴，​​尋復之。

translations.literal: Tie Bao was punished for failure of supervision, stripped of his palace rank, and reduced to second-rank insignia; soon it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Bao was faulted for lax oversight, stripped of his palace rank and reduced to second-rank insignia, which was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 十二年，疏請八旗兵米酌給二成折色，詔斥妄改舊章，革職留任。

translations.literal: In the 12th year he memorialized asking that twenty percent of banner troops' grain rations be commuted to cash; an edict rebuked him for rashly altering old regulations and dismissed him from office while retaining him on duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 12 he proposed commuting twenty percent of banner grain rations to cash payment; the emperor denounced this as a rash change to established rules and dismissed him while keeping him at his post.

sentences.zh: 先後疏論治河，請改建王營減壩，培築高堰、山盱堤后土坡及河岸大堤，修復雲梯關外海口，遣大臣勘議，並採其說施行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized on river control, asking to rebuild the Wangying flood-relief dam, heighten the Gaoyan and Shanxu rear slopes and main river dikes, and restore the estuary beyond Yuntiguan; ministers were sent to survey and discuss, and his proposals were largely adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a series of memorials on river works, urging reconstruction of the Wangying relief dam, strengthening the Gaoyan and Shanxu rear slopes and main embankments, and restoring the estuary beyond Yuntiguan; imperial commissioners surveyed the plans and largely put them into effect.

sentences.zh: 十四年，運河屢壞堤，荷花塘決口合而復潰，鐫級留任。

translations.literal: In the 14th year the Grand Canal dikes broke repeatedly; the breach at Hehuatang was closed and then burst again; his rank was cut but he remained on duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 14 the canal dikes failed repeatedly and the Hehuatang breach, once sealed, opened again; his rank was reduced but he stayed in office.

sentences.zh: 山陽知縣王伸漢冒賑，酖殺委員李毓昌，至是事覺，詔斥鐵保偏聽固執，河工日壞，吏治日弛，釀成重獄，褫職，遣戍烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: Wang Shenhan, magistrate of Shanyang, had embezzled relief funds and poisoned Commissioner Li Yuchang; when the affair came to light, an edict rebuked Tie Bao for partiality and obstinacy, saying river works grew worse daily and official discipline slackened daily, brewing a grave case; he was stripped of office and sent in exile to Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: When it emerged that Shanyang magistrate Wang Shenhan had embezzled relief grain and poisoned Commissioner Li Yuchang, the emperor blamed Tie Bao for partiality and stubbornness, declaring that river works and local government had decayed until a capital crime resulted; Tie Bao was dismissed and exiled to Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 逾年，給三等侍衛，充葉爾羌辦事大臣。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was given the rank of third-class bodyguard and appointed commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made a third-class bodyguard and appointed commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 尋授翰林院侍講學士，調喀什噶爾參贊大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin associate lecturer and transferred to assistant commissioner at Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hanlin associate lecturer and transferred to assistant commissioner at Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 授浙江巡撫，未之任，改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Zhejiang but did not take up the post and was changed to vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was named governor of Zhejiang but never took office and was made vice minister of Personnel instead.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書，調吏部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of Rites and was transferred to head Personnel.

sentences.zh: 請芟吏、兵兩部苛例，條陳時政，多見施行。

translations.literal: He asked to cut harsh precedents in the Ministries of Personnel and War and set forth items on current policy; many were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to prune harsh rules in Personnel and War and laid out policy proposals, many of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 林清之變，召對，極言內監通賊有據，因窮治逆黨，內監多銜恨，遍騰謗言。

translations.literal: At the time of Lin Qing's rebellion he was summoned for audience and strongly stated that eunuchs' collusion with rebels had evidence; because the rebel party was thoroughly prosecuted, many eunuchs bore resentment and spread slander everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: During Lin Qing's uprising he was called in audience and insisted there was proof that eunuchs had aided the rebels; as the conspiracy was pursued to the end, many eunuchs hated him and spread calumny against him.

sentences.zh: 會伊犁將軍松筠劾鐵保前在喀什噶爾治叛裔玉素普之獄，誤聽人言，枉殺回民毛拉素皮等四人，上怒，追念江南李毓昌之獄，斥其屢蹈重咎，褫職，發往吉林效力。

translations.literal: When Ili General Songyun impeached Tie Bao for his earlier trial at Kashgar of the rebel descendant Yusupu, in which he wrongly listened to others and unjustly killed four Muslims including Mulla Supi, the emperor was angry, recalling the Li Yuchang case in Jiangnan, rebuked him for repeatedly falling into grave faults, stripped him of office, and sent him to serve in Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: When Ili General Songyun charged that at Kashgar Tie Bao had, in trying the rebel descendant Yusupu, trusted false reports and wrongly executed four Muslims including Mulla Supi, the emperor, still mindful of the Li Yuchang affair in the south, rebuked him for repeated grave failures, dismissed him, and sent him to Jilin.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，召為司經局洗馬。

translations.literal: In the 23rd year he was summoned as director of studies in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 23 he was recalled as director of studies in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 道光初，以疾乞休，賜三品卿銜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang, on grounds of illness he asked to retire and was granted third-rank ministerial rank as an honorific.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he retired on grounds of illness and was granted honorary third-rank ministerial status.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the 4th year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 4.

sentences.zh: 鐵保慷慨論事，高宗謂其有大臣風。

translations.literal: Tie Bao spoke on affairs with generous forthrightness; Emperor Gaozong said he had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Bao argued his views with bold candor, and the Qianlong Emperor said he had the bearing of a statesman.

sentences.zh: 及居外任，自欲有所表見，倨傲，意為愛憎，屢以措施失當被黜。

translations.literal: When he held provincial posts he wished to make a showing, was haughty, let favor and dislike guide him, and was repeatedly dismissed for mistaken measures.
translations.idiomatic: In provincial office he sought to make his mark, grew arrogant, let personal likes govern his actions, and was repeatedly dismissed for misjudged policies.

sentences.zh: 然優於文學，詞翰並美。

translations.literal: Yet he excelled in letters, and both his prose and poetry were fine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he excelled in belles-lettres, and both his prose and verse were accomplished.

sentences.zh: 兩典禮闈及山東、順天鄉試，皆得人。

translations.literal: Twice he presided over the metropolitan examination and over the Shandong and Shuntian provincial examinations, each time selecting worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: He twice ran the metropolitan examination and the Shandong and Shuntian provincial tests, each time choosing able candidates.

sentences.zh: 留心文獻，為八旗通志總裁。

translations.literal: He attended to documentary sources and served as chief compiler of the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to documentary work as chief compiler of the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 多得開國以來滿洲、蒙古、漢軍遺集，先成白山詩介五十卷，復增輯改編，得一百三十四卷，進禦，仁宗制序，賜名熙朝雅頌集。

translations.literal: He obtained many surviving collections of Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner writers since the founding of the dynasty; first he completed fifty juan of Baishan Shijie, then expanded and revised them to 134 juan, presented them to the throne, and Emperor Renzong wrote a preface and bestowed the title Xichao Yasong Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered many literary remains of Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner writers since the founding, first compiling fifty juan of Baishan Shijie, then expanding them to 134 juan for presentation at court; the Jiaqing Emperor wrote a preface and named the collection Xichao Yasong Ji.

sentences.zh: 自著曰懷清齋集。

translations.literal: His own writings were entitled Huaiqingzhai Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His own collected works were entitled Huaiqingzhai Ji.

sentences.zh: 弟玉保，字閬峰。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu Bao, style name Langfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu Bao, courtesy name Langfeng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年進士，入翰林，有才名。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the 46th year of Qianlong, he entered the Hanlin and had a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 46, he entered the Hanlin and was known for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 高宗親試八旗翰詹，與兄鐵保並被擢，時比以郊、祁，軾、轍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong personally examined the Eight Banner Hanlin and Household officials; he and his elder brother Tie Bao were both promoted together, and people at the time compared them to the Jiao brothers and to Su Shi and Su Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor personally examined Banner Hanlin scholars, he and his brother Tie Bao were promoted together; contemporaries likened them to the Jiao brothers and to Su Shi and Su Zhe.

sentences.zh: 官至兵部侍郎，究心兵家言。

translations.literal: He rose to vice minister of War and devoted himself to military writings.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of War and steeped himself in military theory.

sentences.zh: 川、楚教匪起，嘗原自效行間。

translations.literal: When the sect rebels rose in Sichuan and Hubei, he once volunteered to serve in the field.
translations.idiomatic: When the White Lotus rebellion broke out in Sichuan and Hubei, he once offered to serve at the front.

sentences.zh: 會上欲用為巡撫，為和珅所阻，鬱鬱卒，年甫四十。

translations.literal: Just then the court wished to appoint him governor, but Heshen obstructed it; he died in dejection at barely forty.
translations.idiomatic: The court was about to appoint him governor when Heshen blocked it; he died dispirited at only forty.

sentences.zh: 和瑛，原名和寧，避宣宗諱改，字太葊，額勒德特氏，蒙古鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: He Ying, originally named Hening, changed his name to avoid the taboo of Emperor Xuanzong, style name Taian, of the Erde'ete clan, a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He Ying, born Hening and renamed to avoid the Xuanzong taboo, courtesy name Taian, of the Erde'ete clan, was a Mongol bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年進士，授戶部主事，歷員外郎。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the 36th year of Qianlong, he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and passed through vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Qianlong 36, entered the Ministry of Revenue as a principal clerk, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為安徽太平知府，調潁州。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Taiping in Anhui and was transferred to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Taiping in Anhui, then was transferred to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，擢廬鳳道，歷四川按察使，安徽、四川、陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the 52nd year he was promoted to Luzhou-Fengyang circuit intendant, and successively served as Anhui judicial commissioner and as provincial treasurer of Anhui, Sichuan, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 52 he became Luzhou-Fengyang circuit intendant, then served as judicial commissioner in Sichuan and as provincial treasurer in Anhui, Sichuan, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，予副都統銜，充西藏辦事大臣。

translations.literal: In the 58th year he was given the rank of vice commander of a banner and appointed commissioner in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 58 he was granted a banner vice commander's rank and appointed Tibet commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋授內閣學士，仍留藏辦事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Secretariat academician while remaining to handle affairs in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Secretariat academician while continuing to administer Tibet.

sentences.zh: 和瑛在藏八年，著西藏賦，博採地形、民俗、物產，自為之注。

translations.literal: He Ying spent eight years in Tibet and wrote Xizang Fu, broadly gathering topography, customs, and products, and annotating it himself.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in Tibet he wrote Xizang Fu, drawing widely on geography, customs, and local products, which he annotated himself.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，召為理籓院侍郎，歷工部、戶部，出為山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the 5th year of Jiaqing he was summoned as vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, passed through the Ministries of Works and Revenue, and went out as governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, served in Works and Revenue, and was appointed governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七年，金鄉皁役之孫張敬禮冒考被控，知縣汪廷楷置不問，學政劉鳳誥以聞，下和瑛提鞫，誤聽濟南知府德生言誣斷，為給事中汪鏞所糾。

translations.literal: In the 7th year, Zhang Jingli, grandson of a runner at Jinxian, was accused of impersonation in the examination; Magistrate Wang Tingkai ignored it; Provincial Education Commissioner Liu Fenggao reported it; He Ying was ordered to conduct the inquiry, wrongly listened to Jinan Prefect Desheng, and rendered a false judgment; he was impeached by supervising secretary Wang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 7, Zhang Jingli, grandson of a Jinxian clerk, was accused of examination fraud; Magistrate Wang Tingkai ignored the case until Education Commissioner Liu Fenggao reported it; He Ying was ordered to try it, trusted Jinan prefect Desheng's false account, and was impeached by supervising secretary Wang Yong.

sentences.zh: 上以和瑛日事文墨，廢弛政務，即解職，命鏞從侍郎祖之望往按，得實，褫和瑛職，又以匿蝗災事覺，譴戍烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: The emperor said He Ying daily occupied himself with belles-lettres and neglected government affairs, and immediately removed him; Yong was ordered to follow Vice Minister Zu Zhiwang to investigate; the facts were proved; He Ying was stripped of office; when concealment of a locust disaster also came to light, he was condemned to exile at Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declared that He Ying had neglected government for literary pursuits and dismissed him; Wang Yong joined Vice Minister Zu Zhiwang in investigating, confirmed the charges, and stripped He Ying of office; when a concealed locust disaster also surfaced, he was exiled to Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 尋予藍翎侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣，調喀什噶爾參贊大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the rank of blue-lance bodyguard, served as assistant commissioner at Yarkand, and was transferred to assistant commissioner at Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a blue-lance bodyguard, served as assistant commissioner at Yarkand, and was transferred to Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 九年，授理籓院侍郎，仍留邊任。

translations.literal: In the 9th year he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs while still retaining his frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 9 he was made vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs while keeping his frontier assignment.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「喀什噶爾、英吉沙爾倉儲足供軍食，請減運伊犁布疋，改徵雜糧四千石，減價出糶，且請嗣後折收制錢，以免運費。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'The granaries of Kashgar and Yengisar are sufficient for army provisions; please reduce the transport of cloth bolts to Ili, levy instead four thousand shi of miscellaneous grain, sell it at reduced price, and hereafter collect in standard cash to avoid transport costs.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Kashgar and Yengisar granaries could supply the army, proposing to cut cloth shipments to Ili, levy four thousand shi of grain instead, sell it at reduced rates, and thereafter collect payment in cash to save transport costs.

sentences.zh: 」允之。

translations.literal: ' This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 劾喀喇沙爾歷任辦事大臣私以庫款貸與軍民，及土爾扈特、回子取息錢入己，降革治罪有差。

translations.literal: He impeached successive commissioners at Karashahr for privately lending treasury funds to soldiers and civilians, and for Torghut and Muslim persons taking interest for themselves; demotions, dismissals, and punishments varied by degree.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached successive Karashahr commissioners for lending treasury funds privately to troops and civilians and for Torghuts and Muslims who pocketed interest, with varying demotions and punishments.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召還京為吏部侍郎，調倉場。

translations.literal: In the 11th year he was recalled to the capital as vice minister of Personnel and transferred to the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 11 he was recalled to Beijing as vice minister of Personnel, then put in charge of the capital granaries.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復出為烏魯木齊都統。

translations.literal: Before long he again went out as commander at Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again sent out as commander at Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 十三年，塔爾巴哈台參贊大臣愛星阿欲調瑪納斯戍兵四百人番上屯田，和瑛謂瑪納斯處極邊，戍兵專事操防，不諳耕作，諮駁以聞，上韙之。

translations.literal: In the 13th year, Assistant Commissioner Aixing'a at Tarbagatai wished to rotate four hundred garrison troops at Manas to frontier farming in turn; He Ying said Manas lay at the extreme border, garrison troops were devoted to drill and defense and did not know farming; he consulted and reported a rejection; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 13, Tarbagatai assistant commissioner Aixing'a proposed rotating four hundred Manas garrison troops into farming; He Ying argued that Manas was an extreme frontier post whose troops were trained for defense, not agriculture; his objection was upheld.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the 14th year he was appointed governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 14 he was appointed governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 坐前在倉場失察盜米，降大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Because while at the granary depots he had failed to detect theft of grain, he was demoted to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review for failing to detect grain theft while overseeing the granaries.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷盛京刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the 16th year he was transferred to vice minister of Punishments at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 16 he was transferred to Mukden as vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 復州、寧海、岫岩飢，將軍觀明以匿災罷免，授和瑛為將軍，廉得邊門章京塔清阿等承觀明意，諱災不報，降革有差。

translations.literal: Famine struck Fuzhou, Ninghai, and Xiuyan; General Guan Ming was dismissed for concealing the disaster; He Ying was appointed general; he investigated and found frontier gate secretary Ta Qing'a and others, following Guan Ming's intent, had concealed the disaster and failed to report it; demotions and dismissals varied.
translations.idiomatic: When famine hit Fuzhou, Ninghai, and Xiuyan, General Guan Ming was dismissed for concealing it and He Ying was appointed in his place; he found that frontier secretary Ta Qing'a and others had followed Guan Ming in suppressing reports of the disaster, and punished them with varying demotions.

sentences.zh: 尋以誤捕屯民張建謨為盜，鍛鍊成獄，刑部覆訊雪其冤，議革和瑛職，詔寬之，留任。

translations.literal: Soon, for wrongly arresting colonist Zhang Jianmo as a bandit and forging a case against him, the Ministry of Punishments on re-examination cleared his innocence; it was proposed to dismiss He Ying from office; an edict showed leniency and he remained in post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon faulted for wrongly arresting colonist Zhang Jianmo as a bandit and framing him; when the Ministry of Punishments retried the case and cleared Zhang, dismissal was proposed but the emperor showed leniency and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 調熱河都統，未上，召為禮部尚書，調兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commander at Rehe but had not taken up the post when he was summoned as minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Rehe commander but before taking office was recalled as minister of Rites and then moved to head the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 坐失察盛京宗室裕瑞強娶有夫民婦為妾，降盛京副都統，遷熱河都統。

translations.literal: For failure to supervise when Mukden bannerman Yurui forcibly took a married commoner woman as concubine, he was demoted to vice commander at Mukden and transferred to commander at Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Mukden vice commander for failing to stop bannerman Yurui from forcibly taking a married commoner woman as concubine, then was made Rehe commander.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the 21st year he was appointed minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 21 he was appointed minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 命赴甘肅按倉庫虧缺，得總督先福徇庇及貪縱狀，治如律。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Gansu to investigate shortages in the granaries, found that Governor Xianfu had shown favoritism and conditions of corruption and indulgence, and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Gansu to investigate granary shortfalls, he exposed Governor Xianfu's favoritism and corruption and punished the offenders according to law.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，調兵部，加太子少保，歷禮部、兵部。

translations.literal: In the 22nd year he was transferred to the Ministry of War, given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and passed through the Ministries of Rites and War.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 he moved to the Ministry of War, was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and served in both Rites and War.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，授軍機大臣、領侍衛內大臣，充上書房總諳達、文穎館總裁。

translations.literal: In the 23rd year he was appointed Grand Councilor, chief commandant of the Imperial Bodyguard, chief instructor in the Imperial Study, and chief compiler of the Wenyin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 23 he joined the Grand Council, became chief commandant of the Imperial Bodyguard, headed instruction in the Imperial Study, and served as chief compiler of the Wenyin Hall.

sentences.zh: 逾一歲，調刑部，罷內直。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments and removed from inner service.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Punishments and relieved of inner-court duties.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，卒，贈太子太保，諡簡勤。

translations.literal: In the 1st year of Daoguang he died; he was posthumously given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Jianqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 1 and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Jianqin.

sentences.zh: 和瑛嫺習掌故，優於文學，著書多不傳。

translations.literal: He Ying was well versed in institutional precedents and excelled in letters; many of his books have not been transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He Ying knew court precedent thoroughly and excelled in literature, though many of his writings have not survived.

sentences.zh: 久任邊職，有惠政。

translations.literal: He long held frontier posts and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: His long service on the frontier won him a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 後其子璧昌治回疆，回部猶歸心焉。

translations.literal: Later his son Bichang governed the Muslim frontier, and the Muslim peoples still gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Bichang governed the Muslim frontier, and the local peoples still looked to the family with loyalty.

sentences.zh: 璧昌自有傳。

translations.literal: Bichang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Bichang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 覺羅桂芳，字香東，隸鑲藍旗，總督圖思德孫。

translations.literal: Jueluo Guifang, style name Xiangdong, belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner and was the grandson of Governor Tusi De.
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Guifang, courtesy name Xiangdong, was a Bordered Blue Bannerman and grandson of Governor Tusi De.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the 4th year of Jiaqing, he was selected as a bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Jiaqing 4, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 嘗召對，仁宗曰：「奇才也！

translations.literal: He was once summoned for audience; Emperor Renzong said: 'A rare talent!
translations.idiomatic: Once summoned to audience, the Jiaqing Emperor exclaimed, 'A rare talent!

sentences.zh: 」不數年，累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: ' Within a few years he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: ' Within a few years he rose to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十一年，入直上書房，遷禮部侍郎，歷吏部、戶部侍郎，兼副都統、總管內務府大臣、翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the 11th year he entered the Imperial Study, was transferred to vice minister of Rites, passed through vice ministries of Personnel and Revenue, and concurrently held the posts of vice commander of a banner, superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, and chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 11 he joined the Imperial Study, became vice minister of Rites, then served in Personnel and Revenue while also commanding a banner, heading the Imperial Household Department, and chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 迭典順天、江南鄉試，兼直南書房。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presided over the Shuntian and Jiangnan provincial examinations and concurrently served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly ran the Shuntian and Jiangnan provincial examinations and also served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 桂芳家素貧，有門生餽納，曰：「執贄禮甚古。

translations.literal: Guifang's family had long been poor; when a student offered a gift he said: 'The ritual of presenting tribute is very ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Guifang's family had always been poor; when a student offered a gift he said, 'The ritual of presenting tribute is ancient indeed.

sentences.zh: 某忝佐司農，俸入粗給，無藉乎此。

translations.literal: I am unworthy to assist the Minister of Revenue; my salary roughly suffices; I have no need of this.'
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy to serve in Revenue; my salary is adequate; I have no need of this.'

sentences.zh: 」封還之。

translations.literal: ' He sealed it and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the gift and returned it.

sentences.zh: 大學士祿康輿夫聚博，命偕侍郎英和按治，無所徇。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Lu Kang's wife gathered people for gambling; he was ordered to join Vice Minister Ying He in investigating and punishing, showing favor to none.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Lu Kang's wife was found running gambling gatherings, he was ordered to investigate with Vice Minister Ying He and showed favor to no one.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其不避嫌怨。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for not avoiding enmity and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for fearing neither enmity nor resentment.

sentences.zh: 十八年，教匪林清逆黨闌入禁城，桂芳方直內廷，偕諸王大臣率兵殲捕，敘勞，加二級。

translations.literal: In the 18th year, the rebel party of the sect bandit Lin Qing broke into the Forbidden City; Guifang was then on duty in the inner court; together with the princes and great ministers he led troops to destroy and capture them; for merit he was given two additional ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18, Lin Qing's rebels broke into the Forbidden City while Guifang was on inner-court duty; he joined the princes and ministers in crushing them and was rewarded with two additional ranks.

sentences.zh: 上遇變修省，訓誡臣工，頒御製文七篇，示內廷諸臣，命各抒所見，書以進禦。

translations.literal: After the crisis the emperor cultivated self-examination, admonished his officials, issued seven imperial compositions, showed them to the inner-court ministers, and ordered each to express his views in writing for presentation to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After the crisis the emperor turned inward in reflection, admonished his officials, issued seven imperial essays, showed them to the inner court, and ordered each minister to submit written views.

sentences.zh: 桂芳書罪己詔后曰：「皇上臨御以來，承列聖深仁厚澤，日以愛民為政，四海之內，莫不聞睹。

translations.literal: After the self-reproach edict Guifang wrote: 'Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, inheriting the deep benevolence and thick grace of the successive sage emperors, you have daily made loving the people your government; within the four seas none has failed to hear and see it.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor's self-reproach edict, Guifang wrote: 'Since Your Majesty took the throne, inheriting the deep benevolence of the sage emperors before you, you have governed daily with love for the people, and all within the four seas have witnessed it.

sentences.zh: 今茲事變，豈不怪異？

translations.literal: Now this sudden event—is it not strange?
translations.idiomatic: Yet this sudden crisis—is it not strange?

sentences.zh: 而臣竊以為此未足為聖德之累。

translations.literal: Yet your servant privately thinks this is not enough to count as a burden on sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I privately believe this is not enough to diminish your sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 昔孔子論仁至於濟眾，論敬至於安百姓，皆曰：'堯、舜其猶病諸。

translations.literal: Formerly Confucius, in discussing benevolence up to benefiting the multitude and respect up to securing the common people, said in each case: 'Even Yao and Shun would still find it difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, speaking of benevolence as aiding the multitude and of respect as securing the people, said in each case that even Yao and Shun would still find it difficult.

sentences.zh: '豈真以堯、舜之聖為未至哉？

translations.literal: ' Did he truly mean that the sagehood of Yao and Shun had not been attained?
translations.idiomatic: Did he truly mean that Yao and Shun had not reached sagehood?

sentences.zh: 夫天下之大，萬民之眾，而決其無一夫之梗者，蓋自古其難之。

translations.literal: The realm is vast and the myriad people numerous; to decide that not a single man is recalcitrant has from antiquity been difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast and the people countless; to guarantee that not a single man is disaffected has always been difficult.

sentences.zh: 然而揆之人事，則實有未盡者。

translations.literal: Yet measured against human affairs, there truly were things not fully done.
translations.idiomatic: Yet measured against human affairs, there truly were things left undone.

sentences.zh: 夫林清先以習教被系，既釋歸，轉益煽亂。

translations.literal: Lin Qing was first arrested for practicing the sect teaching; after release he returned home and stirred rebellion all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Qing was first arrested for sect activity; once released, he stirred rebellion all the more.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，往來糾結於曹、衛、齊、魯之間，其黨至數千人。

translations.literal: Within a few years he went back and forth organizing in Cao, Wei, Qi, and Lu; his party reached several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he organized across Cao, Wei, Qi, and Lu until his followers numbered thousands.

sentences.zh: 閹寺職官，竟有與其謀者，而未事之先，曾無一人抉發，是吏無政也。

translations.literal: Eunuch officials actually plotted with him, yet before the affair not one person exposed it—this shows officials had no government.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch officials even plotted with him, yet before the attack not one person exposed the conspiracy—this shows that civil administration had failed.

sentences.zh: 藏利刃，懷白幟，度越門關，飲於都市，無诇而知者，是邏者、門者無禁也。

translations.literal: They hid sharp blades, carried white banners, crossed the gates, drank in the marketplaces, and none who spied knew—this shows patrolmen and gatekeepers had no prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: They hid blades, carried white banners, passed the gates, and drank in the markets without anyone detecting them—this shows that patrolmen and gatekeepers enforced nothing.

sentences.zh: 禁兵千計，賊不及百，闔門而擊之，俄頃可盡，乃兩日一夜始悉擒戮，是軍無律也。

translations.literal: The palace guard numbered over a thousand, the rebels fewer than a hundred; shut the gates and strike them and in a moment they could be finished—yet only after two days and one night were all captured and killed; this shows the army had no discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard numbered over a thousand against fewer than a hundred rebels; with the gates shut they could have been destroyed in moments, yet it took two days and a night to capture and kill them all—this shows the army had no discipline.

sentences.zh: 夫吏惰卒驕，文武並弛，而法制禁令為虛器，則事之可憂，豈獨在賊？

translations.literal: When officials are slack and soldiers arrogant, civil and military alike are lax, and laws, institutions, and prohibitions become empty vessels, then what is to be feared in affairs lies not only in bandits?
translations.idiomatic: When officials grow slack and soldiers arrogant, when civil and military discipline alike relax and laws become empty forms, the danger lies not only in the rebels themselves?

sentences.zh: 我皇上觀微知著，洞悉天下之故，詔曰'方今大弊在因循怠玩'，至哉言乎！

translations.literal: Our emperor, observing the subtle and knowing the manifest, thoroughly understood the causes of the realm, and in an edict said: 'At present the great evil lies in routine and slack indulgence'—how supreme the words!
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor, seeing the subtle and grasping the whole, understood the realm's ills perfectly when he declared in an edict that 'the great evil today is routine and slack indulgence'—how penetrating the words!

sentences.zh: 臣敬繹之，蓋因循怠玩，亦有所由。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully interprets this: routine and slack indulgence also have their sources.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully interpret this: routine and slack indulgence also have their causes.

sentences.zh: 無才與識，則有因循而已；

translations.literal: without talent and knowledge, there is only routine;
translations.idiomatic: without talent and judgment, there is only routine;

sentences.zh: 無志與氣，則有怠玩而已。

translations.literal: without resolve and spirit, there is only slack indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: without resolve and spirit, there is only slack indulgence.

sentences.zh: 是故得人而任之，則因循怠玩之習不患不除。

translations.literal: Therefore if the right man is obtained and entrusted, the habits of routine and slack indulgence need not be feared as impossible to remove.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if the right men are found and entrusted, the habits of routine and slack indulgence can surely be uprooted.

sentences.zh: 儻非其人，微獨不能除其習而已；

translations.literal: if it is not the right man, not only can he not remove the habit;
translations.idiomatic: if it is not the right man, he cannot even remove the habit;

sentences.zh: 就令除之，不因循而且為煩苛，不怠玩而且為躁競，其無裨於治則均耳。

translations.literal: even if he were to remove it, he would not be routine yet would become vexatious and harsh, not slack yet would become rash and contentious—their lack of benefit to good government would be the same.
translations.idiomatic: even if he tried, he would trade routine for vexatious harshness and slackness for rash contention—equally useless to good government.

sentences.zh: 是在皇上詢事考言，循名責實，器使之以奏其能，專任之以收其效，因小失而崇丕業，在陛下一旋轉間耳。

translations.literal: This lies in Your Majesty's inquiring into affairs and examining words, matching names to realities, employing men according to their capacities so they may display their abilities, entrusting them exclusively so as to gather their effects, and through a small setback exalting the great enterprise—all within a single turn of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: This depends on Your Majesty inquiring into affairs, testing words against deeds, matching names to realities, employing each man according to his capacity, entrusting him fully to secure results, and turning a small setback into a greater enterprise—all within a single turn of Your Majesty's will.

sentences.zh: 書行實政論后曰：「實心者何？

translations.literal: After his essay On Practicing Real Government he wrote: 'What is a sincere heart?
translations.idiomatic: In his essay On Practicing Real Government he asked: 'What is a sincere heart?

sentences.zh: 忠是也。

translations.literal: Loyalty is it.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 忠者一於為國，而不亟亟於求上之知。

translations.literal: Loyalty means being single-minded for the state and not urgently seeking the sovereign's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty means single-minded devotion to the state, not urgent pursuit of the sovereign's notice.

sentences.zh: 其所以急於公者如急於己，一政而便於民，其行之而恐不及也；

translations.literal: what makes him urgent for the public as for himself: if a policy benefits the people, he carries it out fearing he may not be in time;
translations.idiomatic: He is as urgent for the public good as for himself: if a policy benefits the people, he implements it fearing he may be too late;

sentences.zh: 一政而不便於民，其去之恐不速也。

translations.literal: if a policy does not benefit the people, he removes it fearing he may not be swift enough.
translations.idiomatic: if a policy harms the people, he removes it fearing he may not be swift enough.

sentences.zh: 不以避疑謗而易其是非之公，不以處疏逖而違其夙夜之志。

translations.literal: He does not, to avoid suspicion and slander, alter the fairness of right and wrong; he does not, because he stands remote and distant, violate his day-and-night resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He does not alter right and wrong to avoid suspicion, nor abandon his day-and-night resolve because he stands at a distance from power.

sentences.zh: 故其於政也，籌之至審，而不為旦夕之謀；

translations.literal: Therefore in government he plans with utmost care and does not scheme for a morning and an evening;
translations.idiomatic: In government he plans with utmost care and does not scheme for short-term gain;

sentences.zh: 行之務當，而不揣詔旨之合；

translations.literal: he carries things out as they ought to be and does not guess whether they match the edict's intent;
translations.idiomatic: he carries policy out as it ought to be done and does not guess whether it matches the edict's intent;

sentences.zh: 惟力是視，不必其事之諒於人；

translations.literal: he looks only to exerting strength and does not require that the affair be understood by others;
translations.idiomatic: he looks only to doing his utmost and does not require that others understand his actions;

sentences.zh: 惟善之從，不必其謀之出於己。

translations.literal: he follows only what is good and does not require that the plan come from himself.
translations.idiomatic: he follows only what is good and does not require that the plan be his own.

sentences.zh: 若是者謂之實政。

translations.literal: One such as this is called real government.
translations.idiomatic: Such a man practices real government.

sentences.zh: 夫為臣之道，疇不當忠，然而忠之實蓋如此。

translations.literal: The way of serving as minister—who ought not to be loyal? Yet the reality of loyalty is truly thus.
translations.idiomatic: Who serving as minister ought not to be loyal? Yet true loyalty is truly thus.

sentences.zh: 非然者，初無寸勞，而已為見功之地；

translations.literal: Those who are not so, though they have not a hair's breadth of labor, already make a place for showing achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Those who are not so, though they have done no real work, already prepare ground to display achievement;

sentences.zh: 未必加譴，而已存巧避之心。

translations.literal: though they may not yet be punished, already harbor a heart of crafty evasion.
translations.idiomatic: though they may not yet be punished, already harbor a heart of crafty evasion.

sentences.zh: 取容於唯諾，而不以國事為憂；

translations.literal: they win favor through yes-and-no compliance and do not take state affairs as a worry;
translations.idiomatic: they win favor through compliant assent and do not worry over state affairs;

sentences.zh: 快意於愛憎，而不以人才為惜。

translations.literal: they take satisfaction in likes and dislikes and do not cherish talent.
translations.idiomatic: they indulge personal likes and dislikes and do not cherish talent.

sentences.zh: 如斯人者，雖我皇上日討而訓之，尚望其能行實政乎？

translations.literal: Men such as these—even if our emperor daily admonishes and instructs them—can one still hope they will practice real government?
translations.idiomatic: Men such as these—even if Your Majesty admonishes them daily—can one still hope they will practice real government?

sentences.zh: 夫政者，上所以治天下之具。

translations.literal: Government is the instrument by which the sovereign governs the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Government is the instrument by which the sovereign governs the realm.

sentences.zh: 然而行之以實，乃能有功，不則文具而已。

translations.literal: Yet only when carried out in reality can it have effect; otherwise it is mere paperwork.
translations.idiomatic: Yet only when carried out in earnest can it achieve results; otherwise it is mere paperwork.

sentences.zh: 官無實政，民乃不治，非細故也。

translations.literal: When officials have no real government, the people are not well governed—this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: When officials practice no real government, the people cannot be well governed—this is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 皇上震動恪恭，求賢納諫，敕中外諸臣，改慮易志。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been stirred to reverent care, sought the worthy and accepted remonstrance, and ordered officials within and without to change their thoughts and alter their resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has been stirred to reverent care, sought the worthy and accepted remonstrance, and ordered officials throughout the empire to change their thoughts and alter their resolve.

sentences.zh: 稍有人心者，疇敢不勉；

translations.literal: those who retain the slightest human heart—who would dare not strive?
translations.idiomatic: those who retain any conscience—who would dare not strive?

sentences.zh: 而臣所欲言者，則又在陛下之心矣。

translations.literal: Yet what your servant wishes to speak lies again in Your Majesty's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I wish to say lies again in Your Majesty's own heart.

sentences.zh: 臣昨歲恭錄乾隆朝臣孫嘉淦三習一弊疏於御製養心殿記冊末，伏原萬幾之暇，時賜觀覽。

translations.literal: Last year your servant respectfully copied at the end of the imperially composed Yangxindian record book the memorial of Qianlong minister Sun Jiagan on Three Habits and One Evil; I humbly pray that amid the myriad affairs Your Majesty may from time to time grant it perusal.
translations.idiomatic: Last year I respectfully copied at the end of the Yangxindian record book Sun Jiagan's Qianlong memorial on Three Habits and One Evil; I humbly pray that amid your myriad duties you may read it from time to time.

sentences.zh: 用其說以考諸臣之政，因以識諸臣之心，則賢才不患其不思奮，庶績不患其不咸熙。

translations.literal: Use its doctrine to examine the officials' government and thereby know the officials' hearts; then worthy talent need not be feared as unwilling to strive, and the myriad tasks need not be feared as failing to flourish together.
translations.idiomatic: Use its doctrine to test officials' conduct and thereby know their hearts; then worthy talent will strive without prompting and the myriad tasks will flourish together.

sentences.zh: 較臣管蠡之見，似更有助於高深焉。

translations.literal: Compared with your servant's narrow view from a tube, it would seem more helpful to lofty depth.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with my narrow view, it would seem more helpful to your lofty purposes.

sentences.zh: 又論致變之源，由於民窮，民窮由於幣輕，幣輕則國與民交病。

translations.literal: He also discussed the source of the crisis as lying in the people's poverty; the people's poverty arose from the lightness of currency; when currency is light, state and people alike fall ill.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the crisis stemmed from popular poverty, that poverty stemmed from debased currency, and that debased currency afflicted both state and people alike.

sentences.zh: 論刑用重典而不得其平，則不能格姦定亂。

translations.literal: He argued that when punishments use severe statutes without obtaining fairness, they cannot reform wickedness and settle disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that harsh punishments applied without fairness cannot reform crime or settle disorder.

sentences.zh: 論民惑邪教，由士大夫好言因果利益有以導之。

translations.literal: He argued that the people's delusion by heterodox teachings arose because scholar-officials liked to speak of karma, retribution, and profit, thereby leading them.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that popular delusion by heterodox sects was led by scholar-officials who delighted in preaching karma, retribution, and profit.

sentences.zh: 因事納規，所言多切中時弊。

translations.literal: Seizing the occasion to offer remonstrance, what he said largely hit the evils of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the occasion to remonstrate, his words largely struck at the evils of the age.

sentences.zh: 於是復條陳時事，或見之，謂其未必盡合上意。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again set forth items on current affairs; some who saw them said they might not entirely accord with the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out further proposals on current affairs; some observers said they might not fully accord with the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 桂芳慨然曰：「此何時，尚以迎合為言耶？

translations.literal: Guifang said with indignation: 'At a time like this, and you still speak of currying favor?
translations.idiomatic: Guifang said indignantly, 'At a time like this, and you still speak of currying favor?

sentences.zh: 」及上，嘉納之，命暫在軍機處學習行走。

translations.literal: ' When it was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it and ordered him temporarily to study and serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: ' When it was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it and ordered him to study temporarily in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，軍事竣，以贊畫功賜桂芳子炳奎七品小京官。

translations.literal: In the 19th year, when military affairs were concluded, for planning merit Guifang's son Bingkui was granted a seventh-rank junior capital official post.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19, when the campaigns ended, Guifang's son Bingkui was granted a seventh-rank capital post for his father's planning merit.

sentences.zh: 尋命往廣西按事，授漕運總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to go to Guangxi to investigate affairs and was appointed director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to Guangxi to investigate affairs and was appointed director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 未至廣西，於武昌途次病疫，卒。

translations.literal: Before reaching Guangxi, on the road at Wuchang he fell ill with epidemic disease and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching Guangxi he contracted plague on the road at Wuchang and died.

sentences.zh: 上以桂芳明慎直爽，方鄉用，至是優詔褒卹，嘆為「良才難得」，贈太子少保，加尚書銜；

translations.literal: The emperor, because Guifang was clear, cautious, direct, and frank, and had just been about to employ him in the provinces, now issued a favorable edict of praise and condolence, sighing that "worthy talent is hard to obtain," posthumously granting him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and adding ministerial rank;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who had valued Guifang's clarity, caution, and frankness and was about to employ him in the provinces, issued a generous edict of praise and condolence, sighing that "worthy talent is hard to find," and posthumously made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with ministerial rank;

sentences.zh: 復以曾授三阿哥讀書，喪至京師，命三阿哥往奠，御製詩悼之，諡文敏。

translations.literal: also because he had once taught the Third Imperial Son, when the coffin reached the capital the Third Son was ordered to offer libation; the emperor composed an elegy and gave the posthumous name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: because he had once taught the Third Imperial Son, when the coffin reached Beijing the prince was ordered to offer libation; the emperor composed an elegy and gave the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 著有經進、敬儀堂詩存，才華豐贍，為時所稱。

translations.literal: His works include Jingjin and Jingyitang Shicun; his talent was rich and ample and was praised by his age.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Jingjin and Jingyitang Shicun; his literary talent was abundant and widely praised.

sentences.zh: 論曰：承平既久，八旗人士起甲科、列侍從者，亦多以文字被恩眷。

translations.literal: The commentator says: After long peace, among Eight Banner men who rose through the civil examinations and entered attendance, many also received imperial favor through letters.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator observes: After long peace, many Bannermen who rose through the examinations and entered court attendance also won imperial favor through literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 達椿忤權相，晚乃見用，其守正有足稱。

translations.literal: Da Chun offended the powerful minister and was employed only late in life; his upholding of rectitude is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Da Chun offended the powerful minister and was employed only late in life; his steadfast integrity deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 鐵保、和瑛並器識淵雅，述作斐然。

translations.literal: Tie Bao and He Ying alike had deep capacity and elegant discernment, and their writings were brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Bao and He Ying alike possessed deep discernment and elegant learning, and their writings were brilliant.

sentences.zh: 桂芳通達政體，建言諤諤，最為一時俊才，年命不永，未竟其用，惜哉！

translations.literal: Guifang understood government thoroughly, remonstrated with blunt loyalty, and was foremost among the outstanding talents of the age; his years were not long, he did not fulfill his use—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Guifang understood government thoroughly and remonstrated with blunt loyalty; he was the foremost talent of his age, yet his life was short and his promise unfulfilled—alas!
